title: PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.collide_shape returns incorrect collision points based on motion
body:
### Tested versions

Godot version: v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Mac OS 10.15.7 (Catalina) - a very old macbook pro from 2012.

### Issue description

I'm getting strange or incorrect values back from collide_shape. Please see the example scene below.
From my understanding of the docs, collision_test takes the motion value of the space query into account. This can be verified in the example below by replacing the motion in the query with zero - no collisions occur.
The expectation is that the collision points are in the path of the motion. Instead, the collision point on the collided body is on the outside of the shape along the vector passing through the centre of both shapes, which can be entirely outside the path of the motion.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6162a055-c3f2-4f39-ba13-311a7aba224a

If this result is expected, I'm not sure how useful it is, and I don't think that the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_physicsdirectspacestate2d.html#class-physicsdirectspacestate2d-method-collide-shape) makes it clear at all. In fact, the documentation doesn't really make sense (particularly the second part) and should be rewritten imo.

### Steps to reproduce

Set up a PhysicsShapeQueryParameters2D with a shape and some motion, such that the position and motion of the shape causes it to collide with another shape. Pass this information into PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D.collide_shape, and observe that the returned collision points can be in unintuitive places.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)


Example project

[collision-test-1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18623498/collision-test-1.zip)
